items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Fats Waller was in Connie’s Inn.

ctx.x: No. We’re playing. We ain’t doing nothing. We go on the road and come back stranded two or three times. Got that rent to pay. Them people don’t want to hear nothing about where you’ve been on the road and all that business. Man want his rent. So my uncle Paul called down and asked how I was doing, because he’s like a father to me. Said, “Tell him I’m’a call him, call on him. I want to talk to him.” I got on the phone. We talked. Can’t go into details on that, but we talked. He said, “What’cha doing?” I said, “I…

So I go to New York. Now there’s Chick Webb on the Savoy. Fletcher Henderson is at Roseland. And Jelly Roll had left Rosemont. There was Charlie Johnson at Smalls’ Paradise. Fats Waller was in Connie’s Inn. Chick Webb was on the Savoy. Charlie Johnson was at Smalls’ Paradise. The city just lit up with musicians. People . . . it is the beginning of the fall. It’s September or October. Everybody’s well dressed, well groomed, wearing the fashion clothes. In the evening everybody going to the restaurant down Seventh…
He was kind of tall, and he smiled all the time. But he had a strange name. He would be in there. And James P. Johnson would come through there. Fats Waller come through there.

Jelly Roll stood on the corner. They didn't understand Jelly Roll. Jelly Roll would be talkin' like he talked to night people, who understand Jelly Roll... Jelly Roll would stand out in front of the club and talk to all these defeated musicians; half of them couldn't play, including me. We'd stand around there waiting for a gig and looking up at Jelly Roll. Well, Jelly Roll is from home. But Jelly Roll, he loves an audience. I noticed Jelly Roll had two little things on the end of his jaw that he could establish…

items.title: Danny Barker Interview (Louis Armstrong memorial broadcast), 1971-07-09
items.q: You've seen Fats Waller come on, doing his humor.

ctx.x: The music is considered singers. Oh, I see. But then you become a stylist. I see what you're saying. See, with Larry coming on, you become an individual stylist. So people say, well, he always sings cute. See, like, whole Carmichael, people will buy his records. He's got a little thing like something about China, a nice little record. Well, you like it. Yeah, he was really reciting to his music, really. He's not a guy, but he's a stylist. I see what you're saying. You've seen Fats Waller come on, doing his humor.…

...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... If you've never seen a quaint old southern city Just think of noon or noon And if you haven't seen that town, boy It's a pity There's nothing like New Orleans It will remind you of old-fashioned lace A glass of wine will greet your smiling face And if you've ever seen a brown-eyed gal like my boy You down and do I need you Mm-hmm . . . . . . . . . . . . .…
